prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place in the story of Sennacherib's invasion of Judah, 2 Kings 18-19
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in the story of Sennacherib's invasion of Judah in 2 Kings 18-19: Lachish, Samaria, the conquered cities his envoys boasted of (Hamath, Arpad, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph), Egypt and Tirhakah king of the Nile land of Cush, Nineveh, and the land of Armenia where his killers fled
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay in today's Sudan, so modern Ethiopia is not counted. Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine).
prompts.summary: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year Sennacherib of Assyria took Judah's fenced cities and besieged Lachish. His officer Rabshakeh mocked trust in Egypt and listed the gods of conquered cities. Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah prophesied, and the angel of the Lord smote the Assyrian camp; Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where his sons slew him (2 Kgs 18-19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Sennacherib took the fenced cities of Judah and camped at Lachish, then sent his army against Jerusalem (2 Kgs 18:13-17).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Rabshakeh mocked Judah's trust in Egypt, that bruised reed (2 Kgs 18:21).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: After the angel smote the camp, Sennacherib went home and dwelt at Nineveh (2 Kgs 19:35-36).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: His envoys asked where the gods of Hamath and Arpad were, and named Gozan and Rezeph among lands Assyria destroyed (2 Kgs 18:34; 19:12).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: They also asked whether any god had delivered Samaria (2 Kgs 18:34).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Haran is among the places they boasted of destroying (2 Kgs 19:12); Bible Dictionary Haran places it near the source of the Euphrates.

answers.name: Armenia
answers.fact: His sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smote him and escaped into the land of Armenia (2 Kgs 19:37); Bible Dictionary Ararat: the district the Assyrians called Urartu, now called Armenia.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Tirhakah king of Ethiopia marched out to fight him (2 Kgs 19:9); Bible Ethiopia was the Nile land south of Egypt.

prompts.display_text: Pin an independent South American country in the land Melvin J. Ballard dedicated for preaching in 1925.
prompts.text_original: On Christmas Day 1925 in Buenos Aires, apostle Melvin J. Ballard dedicated all of South America for the preaching of the gospel. Pin any independent country of South America.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Bolivia, Uruguay, Venezuela)
prompts.note: The prayer covered the whole continent, so every South American country counts. French Guiana is part of France and does not.
prompts.summary: In late 1925 Elder Melvin J. Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles arrived in Buenos Aires to open a South American mission. On December 25 he dedicated the whole continent for the preaching of the gospel. Global Histories chronologies across the continent record that 1925 prayer as the start of Church growth in South America.

answers.fact: Ballard offered the prayer in Buenos Aires in December 1925.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city or town named in Acts 18, from Paul's stay in Corinth to Apollos at Ephesus
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city or town named in Acts 18, the chapter of Paul's stay in Corinth and his return to Antioch
prompts.note: Only cities count, not regions, so Syria and North Macedonia do not. Antioch is in Turkey.
prompts.summary: Acts 18 covers Paul's long stay in Corinth, where he made tents with Aquila and Priscilla, Jews expelled from Rome. He sailed from Cenchrea to Ephesus, landed at Caesarea, and went down to Antioch. Meanwhile Apollos of Alexandria arrived at Ephesus and was taught the way of God more perfectly.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul left Athens for Corinth, stayed a year and a half, and shaved his head in Cenchrea (Acts 18:1, 11, 18).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Claudius had commanded all Jews to leave Rome, so Aquila and Priscilla came to Corinth (Acts 18:2).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Paul landed at Caesarea and went up to salute the church; he hoped to keep the feast at Jerusalem (Acts 18:21-22).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Paul reasoned at Ephesus, then went down to Antioch, today's Antakya (Acts 18:19-22).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Apollos, mighty in the scriptures, was born at Alexandria (Acts 18:24).

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American mainland country whose first General Authority from that country was called between 1981 and 1991
prompts.text_original: In the 1980s Latin American members began to be called as General Authorities. A Latin American mainland country (Mexico, Central America or Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking South America) whose first native General Authority was called between 1981 and 1991.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Latin American mainland); Church News 1989, 1991 and 2021
prompts.note: Later firsts include Uruguay (Francisco J. Vinas, 1996), Venezuela (Rafael E. Pino, 2008) and Peru (Juan A. Uceda, 2010).
prompts.summary: Angel Abrea of Argentina became the first General Authority from South America in 1981. Brazil followed in 1985, Mexico and Guatemala in 1989 as the Second Quorum of the Seventy was formed, Chile in 1990 and Colombia in 1991. Each call showed the Church's leadership growing with its Latin American membership.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Horacio A. Tenorio, the first General Authority of Mexican ancestry, was sustained to the Second Quorum of the Seventy, April 1, 1989.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Angel Abrea was called to the First Quorum of the Seventy in April 1981, the first General Authority from South America.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Helio da Rocha Camargo was called as a General Authority Seventy, April 6, 1985.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Eduardo Ayala became the first Chilean General Authority Seventy, March 31, 1990.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Carlos H. Amado was called as a General Authority Seventy, April 1, 1989.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Julio E. Davila, Colombia's first stake president, was sustained to the Second Quorum of the Seventy, April 6, 1991, the first General Authority from Colombia.
